record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Let G=(V,E) be a graph and let k≥0. A set Z⊂V is an (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing set if, for every set E' of at most k edges, Z remains a zero-forcing set for the graph (V,E\E'). For sparse graphs resembling power-grid networks, determine whether one can give a structural characterization of the minimum-size (n−k)-contingent zero-forcing sets, in particular for graphs with few cycles or for sparse graphs of large diameter.

evidence.quote: Definition 7.3 ((n − k)-contingent Zero Forcing). Given a graph G = (V, E), a set Z ⊆ V is a (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set if for every set of edges E0 of size at most k, Z is a zero-forcing set for G0 = (V, E − E0).
Open Problem 7.1. Is there a structural characterization of the minimal-sized (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing sets for graphs with few cycles? For sparse graphs with large diameter?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with $n=|V|$. Recall the standard zero-forcing color-change rule: starting from a set $Z\subseteq V$ of initially blue vertices (all others being white), repeatedly apply the rule that if a blue vertex has exactly one white neighbor, then that white neighbor becomes blue. The set $Z$ is a zero-forcing set for $G$ if iterating this rule eventually colors all of $V$ blue.

Fix an integer $k\ge 0$. A set $Z\subseteq V$ is called an $(n-k)$-contingent zero-forcing set for $G$ if, for every set $E'\subseteq E$ with $|E'|\le k$, the set $Z$ is still a zero-forcing set for the graph $G'=(V,E\setminus E')$. Let $Z_{n-k}(G)$ denote the minimum cardinality of such a set.

Problem: Provide a structural characterization of the minimum-size $(n-k)$-contingent zero-forcing sets for sparse graph classes. In particular:
(a) characterize these minimum sets for graphs with few cycles (e.g., trees, unicyclic graphs, and more generally graphs whose cyclomatic number is bounded);
(b) characterize these minimum sets for sparse graphs of large diameter.
artifact.status_search_result: No published structural characterization of minimum $(n-k)$-contingent zero-forcing sets for sparse graphs with few cycles or large diameter was found. Related work studies constrained / leaky / failed zero forcing variants and resilient strong structural controllability, but none provides such a characterization. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Resilient Strong Structural Controllability in Networks using Leaky Forcing in Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies leaky/contingent forcing variants relevant to robustness in power-grid-like networks but does not give a structural characterization of minimum-size (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing sets.
status_evidence.claim: Related variant studied; main open problem on structural characterization not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Deduction, Constrained Zero Forcing, and Constrained Searching
status_evidence.snippet: Provides equivalences and complexity results for constrained zero forcing but does not characterize minimum (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing sets in sparse low-cycle or large-diameter graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Constrained zero forcing studied in different sense; question remains open.
